as_told.title: Project Sign Estimate of the Situation rejected by Vandenberg

plain: In the late 1940s, staff at Project Sign, the US Air Force's first UFO study, based at Wright Field in Ohio, are said to have written a top-secret report concluding that UFOs were craft from another world. The report was called the Estimate of the Situation, and the story goes that the Air Force general Hoyt Vandenberg killed it. Jesse Michels tells it in his own words, dating the report to 1949. Robert Salas, a former Air Force officer, tells it too, but dates it to 1948 and says Vandenberg rejected the report rather than burning it. Salas insists "it was a real document," and adds that it "was seen by Ruppelt." That is Edward Ruppelt, who later ran the Air Force's UFO study. Salas cites Ruppelt's book, The Report on Unidentified Flying Objects, as his source. If true, it would mean Air Force investigators concluded early on that UFOs were extraterrestrial and that the conclusion was buried from the top.
